title: Beef Wellington
summary: A showstopper for five. Most of the work is done the day before, so assembly day is manageable.

steps.heading: Day 1: the night before
steps.text: Sear the beef fillet all over in a hot pan with olive oil, {timer:2} per side, until golden. Leave to cool completely, brush with the Dijon mustard and refrigerate.

For the duxelles, finely chop the mushrooms and cook them in batches over a high heat with the thyme and olive oil, until all the moisture has evaporated and the mixture is dry. Leave to cool, then refrigerate.

For the red wine sauce, roast the beef trimmings, add the chopped shallots and deglaze with the red wine. Reduce by half, then add the beef stock and simmer for {timer:60|sauce}. Strain and refrigerate.
If you are wrapping the beef in savoury crepes, make them now (see the Savoury Crepes recipe).

steps.heading: Day 2: assembly, 3–4 hours before serving
steps.text: Lay a large sheet of cling film on the work surface. If using crepes, lay them on it, overlapping.
Spread the duxelles over the cling film, or over the crepes if using, and lay the Parma ham slices on top.
Place the beef fillet in the centre and use the cling film to roll everything tightly around it into a sausage shape. Twist the ends to seal and chill for {timer:15}, until it has set.
Roll the puff pastry out into a large rectangle. Unwrap the beef parcel onto the pastry, wrap the pastry around it, seal the edges with egg wash and score the top decoratively.
Brush the whole surface with the remaining egg yolk. Refrigerate for {timer:30}.
Bake at {temp:200} for {timer:20-25}, until the pastry is golden and the internal temperature reaches {temp:52-55!} for medium-rare.
Rest for {timer:15-20}. Slice the Wellington into thick portions and serve with the red wine sauce and Orange Asparagus.

tips: Temperature is critical: aim for 52–55 °C inside for medium-rare, and use a meat thermometer. A single fillet cooks slightly faster than two separate ones. A traditional Wellington uses savoury crepes as a moisture barrier between the duxelles and the pastry, but they are optional. Pair it with a full-bodied red such as Cabernet Sauvignon, Bordeaux or Syrah. For clean slices, use a very sharp knife and wipe it between cuts.
Serve with Orange Asparagus, and use Savoury Crepes for wrapping if you like.
